summary.text: The module failed to activate the audio session or to start the media playback service.
The client that requested the activation. For a hold, it is the key that was passed to
`holdSession`

. For any other client, it is the name that the media library registered. When the
media playback service fails on Android, it is the ID of the Now Playing owner, or
`Now Playing`
when no owner exists.
What failed, why, and what to do next.

The app-wide audio policy. The media libraries that use this module read it to configure audio
focus on Android and the shared audio session on iOS.
Whether the session allows recording. On iOS, this selects the
`playAndRecord`

category. On
Android, the value is advisory: the module does not change the system audio state for it, and
media libraries read it.

How the app's audio behaves next to audio from other apps. A media library can request a
stricter mode for one use, but never a looser one.

Whether the app plays audio while the iOS silent switch is on. On Android, the module reports
the ringer state to media libraries, and they apply this value.

Whether audio keeps playing when the app goes to the background. The module does not enforce
this value: media libraries read it and apply it to their players. Background playback also
needs the [
`supportsBackgroundPlayback`
](#configurable-properties) config plugin option.

Whether audio plays through the earpiece instead of the speaker. On iOS, this only has an
effect when
`allowsRecording`
is
`true`
(that is, the audio session category is
`playAndRecord`
). When
`false`

(the default), audio is routed through the speaker. On Android,
this value has no effect.

An interruption of the app's audio began or ended.

An interruption that began can end with at most one
`ended`
event before the next
`began`

. A
permanent loss of audio focus may never end.
Why the system interrupted the app's audio.
The interruption began.
Whether the interrupted playback can resume. It is
`true`

only when a media library or a
hold still uses the session and the session is active again.
The interruption ended.

Describes how the app's audio behaves next to audio from other apps.

-
`mixWithOthers`

: The app's audio plays together with other apps' audio.
-
`duckOthers`

: Other apps lower their volume while the app plays.
-
`doNotMix`

: Other apps pause while the app plays, and they can resume when it stops.
-
`doNotMixPersistent`

: Other apps pause while the app plays, and they do not resume by
themselves. On Android, the module requests permanent audio focus. On iOS, the module does not
notify other apps when the session deactivates.

Why the system interrupted the app's audio. The set can grow, so handle unknown values.

-
`default`

: Another app or a system event, such as a call, took the audio. Android reports only
this reason.
-
`routeDisconnected`

: The output device disconnected (iOS 17 and later only).
-
`builtInMicMuted`
: The built-in microphone was muted (iOS only).
The audio route changed.
Why the route changed.

Why the audio route changed. The set can grow, so handle unknown values.

-
`oldDeviceUnavailable`

: The previous output device, such as headphones, disconnected. Android
reports only this reason.
-
`newDeviceAvailable`

: A new output device connected (iOS only).
-
`categoryChange`

: The session category changed (iOS only).
-
`other`
: Any other route change (iOS only).

Adds a listener for failures to activate the audio session or to start the media playback
service.

Adds a listener for interruptions of the app's audio, such as a phone call or another app taking
audio focus.

On Android, the module learns about interruptions from audio focus, and it requests no focus when
the effective interruption mode is
`mixWithOthers`

, which is the default. The module calls the
listener only in the other modes, and only while a media library or a hold uses the session.

On iOS, the module can send
`began`

while no media library uses the session.

On web, the module never calls the listener.

Adds a listener for audio route changes, such as headphones connecting or disconnecting.

On Android, the module reports only
`oldDeviceUnavailable`

, when the output device disconnects.
It does not report a device that connects.

On web, the module never calls the listener.
Gets the current app-wide audio policy.
Keeps the audio session active, or audio focus held on Android, until you call
`releaseSession`

with the same key. Use it to keep the session active between two sounds. A second call with a
key that is already held begins the hold again. Use that to activate the session again after an
`activationError`

or an interruption. The module releases every hold when the JavaScript runtime
reloads.

The call returns at once. If the activation fails, the module sends an
`activationError`

event.
On web, it does nothing.
A name for the hold. The
`activationError`
event reports it as its
`client`
Releases the hold that
`holdSession`

created with the same key. The module deactivates the
session 1 second after the last use or hold ends, except in
`mixWithOthers`

mode on iOS, where it
never deactivates the session automatically. An unknown key does nothing.
The key that was passed to
`holdSession`

Updates the app-wide audio policy. Fields that the update leaves out keep their current values.
The module applies the new policy to the active session, and media libraries read it for every
later use.

On web, the module stores the policy and does not change browser audio.

content.text:
A promise that resolves when the module accepted the policy. On iOS, it rejects when the
merged policy is invalid, for example
. The error message says how to fix the policy.

summary.text: The fields of the audio policy to change.
